Q: HTML: set onclick event handler in external script file before user clicks it? A:

If you embed the script element after the input field, then you don't need $(document).ready to begin with.

After you removed that, any delay should be minimal, if still existent at all. If you want to be absolutely on the safe side - then add disabled to your submit button in the initial HTML, and then enable the button again via your JavaScript.

Q: Using a regex lookahead after spaces A:

Warning

This answer is just regarding the regex question, not the JSON parsing, to be clear for everybody. This will never handle proper JSON, which will certainly not be on several lines and indented like expected. Using a JSON5 parser seems to be the way to go in any case.

Answer about the regex only

I would personnally not use .*? to match the JSON key/property but instead use \w+. As . can be anything, you won't help the regex engine be efficient.

No need to use a negative lookbehind either, as we known that we have spaces and then a key/property, which can't use special chars. So I would come up with this:

/^(\s*)(\w+)\s*:/gmu

Or with named capturing groups:

/^(?<indent>\s*)(?<word>\w+)\s*:/gmu

  • ^(\s*) is to capture the spaces before the key/property so that we can put them back in the replacement value.

  • (\w+) is the unquoted value which you want to quote.

  • \s*: is to match eventually spaces and the : char.

  • I activated the unicode flag, as you will probably have unicode content in the JSON you are correcting.

Play with it here: https://regex101.com/r/tlxcnM/1

const sample = `
  unquoted: "this is the first",
  "quoted": "this is the second"
`;
const result = sample.replaceAll(
  /^(?<indent>\s*)(?<word>\w+)\s*:/gmu,
  '$<indent>"$<word>":'
);
console.log(result);
